History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old man with history of anxiety presents with an acute, severe left-sided headache since 05:30 this morning; features suggest tension-type vs. migraine. No red-flag features identified. Advised NSAID trial, hydration, sleep optimisation, stress reduction, counselling referral, and 1-week follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset severe headache, left side of head, woke patient from sleep at 05:30 today.  
• Course: Persistent throughout the day; Paracetamol provided no relief. Slightly eases after initial discomfort when lying down.  
• Character/previous episodes: Prior headaches described as milder “cluster at the front,” never this severe or unilateral.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia; transient dizziness on waking (resolved). Denies neck stiffness, fever, nausea, vomiting.  
• Triggers/relieving factors: Ongoing work-related stress and late nights for ~2 months; no clear physical triggers identified; lying down eventually helps.  
• Review of systems: No visual aura, focal neurologic deficits, speech changes, weakness, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, or recent head trauma reported.

Past Medical History:
• Generalised Anxiety Disorder (diagnosed ~2 years ago); currently managed with Sertraline.  
• No hypertension or other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
• Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol – self-administered today; dose not documented.  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies (NKDA).

Social History:
• Lives with partner; owns a cat.  
• Non-smoker; alcohol/substance use not discussed.  
• Exercises: runs ~3×/week.  
• Diet: “OK,” not particularly healthy or unhealthy.  
• Work: Significant stress and backlog for ~2 months; frequently works late nights.

Family History:
• Mother with anxiety.  
• No family history of migraine or other major illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed (telephone consult).

Investigations:
• None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache – likely tension headache vs. migraine.  
  • Initiate Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as first-line per current guidance; may continue Paracetamol.  
  • Provide patient handout on headache red-flag symptoms; low threshold to re-contact if any develop or pain worsens.  
  • Consider blood tests/imaging if no improvement or if red-flags emerge.

Issue 2: Contributing work-related stress/fatigue.  
  • Recommend self-certified sick leave (~1 week).  
  • Encourage minimum 7–8 h sleep nightly, hydration 1.5–2 L water/day (excluding caffeine).  
  • Provide counselling service link for self-referral; advised to explore stress-management strategies.

Issue 3: Chronic anxiety.  
  • Continue Sertraline.  
  • Monitor mental health; no current suicidal ideation.  
  • Reinforce availability of GP support if anxiety worsens.

General Plan:
• Arrange follow-up appointment in 1 week with GP to assess headache response and review need for further work-up.  
• Provide written consult summary and resources via patient portal.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No vitals, neurological or fundoscopic examination, medication dosages, or exact Ibuprofen regimen documented.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; no significant inaudible sections.
